diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence, $(\qa[1] + \qa[2]) \sim (\qb[1] + \qb[2])$, that is there exists a nonzero quaternion $\qq$ such that
Substituting \eqref{eq:PAIRWISE_SIMILARITY_PROOF_PART_1} into \eqref{eq:SUM_SIMILARITY} yields $\qq[][-1]\qa[2]\qq[] = \qb[2]$, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (SUM_SIMILARITY) holds for some q delivered by the similarity of the sums. The proof then builds a new q = q_1 q_2, with q_2 constrained only to commute with b_1. It substitutes this q into (SUM_SIMILARITY) as if it were the old q. Nothing shows that q_1 q_2 satisfies (SUM_SIMILARITY). One needs a common solution of q^{-1}a_1 q = b_1 and q^{-1}(a_1+a_2)q = b_1+b_2, and finding it is the content of the lemma. Counterexample to the step: a_1=b_1=i, a_2=b_2=j. Then q=i+j satisfies (SUM_SIMILARITY) but sends i to j, and it is not of the form q_1 q_2 with q_2 commuting with i. The proof also applies the similarity lemma to a_1+a_2, which may be real, although that lemma is stated only for nonreal quaternions. The lemma's statement is true, but the converse proof is incomplete.

failure_location.quote: Set $\qq = \qq[1]\qq[2]$, where $\qq[2]$ is a nonzero quaternion such that $\qb[1]\qq[2] = \qq[2]\qb[1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose q_2 explicitly in the centralizer of b_1, i.e. as a rotation about the axis b_1 taking q_1^{-1}a_2 q_1 to b_2. This is possible because both have the same norm and the same inner product with b_1. Alternatively, argue directly with Gram matrices of the imaginary parts. Also treat the case where a_1+a_2 is real.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit criterion for pairwise similarity (similar pairs plus equal Re(a_1 a_2)) is not established in the 'if' direction. This is the only non-tautological form of the paper's claimed necessary and sufficient condition for f=0. Theorem 4.4 as stated is tautological by definition, and the later proofs use only the forward direction.
issues.title: Converse of pairwise-similarity characterization conflates two different quaternions q
issues.why_classification: The statement survives and a contained replacement argument fixes it. No new global architecture is needed, but the missing step is the substance of the converse.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\qq$ be a solution of \eqref{eq:WAHBAS_EQUATION}. Then, it holds
and hence \eqref{eq:HOMOGENEOUS_WAHBAS_EQUATION_PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS}, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof starts from a solution of f(q)=0 and derives (PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS). That is only the implication 'f=0 implies (PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS)'. The converse is never shown: that q^{-1}a_1 q=b_1 and q^{-1}(a_1×a_2)q=b_1×b_2 force q^{-1}a_2 q=b_2. The converse needs a real argument. Conjugation by q preserves cross products and dot products, so one applies it to a_1×(a_1×a_2) and uses the data equalities |a_1|=|b_1| and Re(a_1 a_2)=Re(b_1 b_2). The collinear case a_1×a_2=0 needs separate handling.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the converse by the cross-product-preservation argument above, with a separate treatment of the collinear case. Alternatively, weaken the lemma to a one-way implication and verify sufficiency in Theorem 4.6 directly.
issues.overall_effect: Only the implication 'f=0 implies (PERPENDICULAR_COMPONENTS)' is supported, and the necessity part of Theorem 4.6 uses just that. The 'equivalent' claim, and any sufficiency argument for the parametrization built on it, is unsupported.
issues.title: Equivalence claimed in the perpendicular-components lemma, but only one implication is proved
issues.why_classification: The converse is a short, routine argument, or the claim can be reduced to the implication actually used, without loss of the paper's results.

issues.failure_explanation: Nothing excludes parallel observations. Take a_1=i, a_2=2i, b_1=j, b_2=2j, which are pairwise similar. Then a_1×a_2=b_1×b_2=0, so a_3=b_3=0. The proof invokes a_3 ~ b_3 and Theorem 3.3 for the Sylvester equation a_3 q_2 = q_2 b_3. Both require nonreal (nonzero) a_3, b_3, and Lemma 3.1 requires a nonzero radicand. The formula (Q2) gives q_2 = λ_2·sqrt(0) = 0, hence q = 0. Yet the solution set is nonempty: it is q_1(α+β b_1), a two-parameter family. So the stated 'general solution' is wrong or undefined in this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Im a_1 × Im a_2 ≠ 0 to the theorem. Add a separate statement for the collinear case: q = q_1 q_2 with q_2 any nonzero element of {α+β Im b_1}, with q_1 from (Q1).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed complete parametrization of all zero-cost quaternions fails for collinear pairs of observations. This is a degenerate case that the hypotheses explicitly allow.
issues.title: Closed-form solution breaks down for collinear observations (a_1 x a_2 = 0)
issues.why_classification: A contained extra case and an added hypothesis fix it. The method and the rest of the result are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition q_2 b_1 = b_1 q_2 must hold for the whole q_2 = λ_2 sqrt(a_3 b_3^*) + μ_2(a_3+b_3). The proof evaluates the commutator only on the μ_2 term and silently drops λ_2[sqrt(a_3 b_3^*), b_1]. In the generic case this term vanishes, but that needs an argument. Both a_3 and b_3 are perpendicular to b_1, so a_3 b_3^* is real plus a multiple of b_1, and its root commutes with b_1. In the case a_3 = -b_3, the root is an arbitrary pure p, and the stated side condition only forces p ⟂ a_3. Commutation with b_1 additionally requires p ∥ b_1. Counterexample: a_1=b_1=i, a_2=b_2=j, q_1=2i. The radicand is negative real, so q_2=j is allowed. Then q=q_1 q_2 is a multiple of k, and k^{-1} i k = -i ≠ b_1, so f(q)≠0. The theorem also uses q_1^* instead of q_1^{-1}. That changes the radicand by |q_1|^2 (harmless for the root up to λ_2), but the side-condition equality 'q_1^*(...)q_1 = -b_1×b_2' is then wrong unless |q_1|=1. Finally, the proof shows only necessity. It never verifies that every parametrized q solves f=0, which 'general solution' requires.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove that sqrt(a_3 b_3^*) commutes with b_1, using a_3, b_3 ⟂ b_1. In the case a_3 = -b_3, replace the side condition by q_2 = λ_2 Im b_1 (λ_2≠0), and use q_1^{-1} in that condition. Then verify directly that every parametrized q satisfies both alignments.
issues.overall_effect: The stated parametrization contains non-solutions in the case a_3 = -b_3, so it is not the set of zero-cost quaternions there. Even in the generic case, necessity and sufficiency of the formula are not fully proved.
issues.title: Commutation of q_2 with b_1 not imposed on the lambda_2-term; extra non-solutions when a_3 = -b_3; sufficiency unverified
issues.why_classification: The structure of the result stays the same. The repair is a contained argument plus a corrected side condition in one degenerate sub-case.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this paper, we solve the Wahba's problem for the special and practically important case $\ell = 2$.
We present a closed-form solution to Wahba's problem in the quaternion domain for the special case of two vector observations.
thereby improving computational efficiency and analytical clarity of the solution

issues.failure_explanation: Wahba's problem is the minimization of f over q. The paper treats only f(q)=0, i.e. exact data with (a_1,a_2) ~ (b_1,b_2), via Theorems 4.4 and 4.6. For two observations that are not pairwise similar, f has no zero. The minimizer is not characterized at all, and no result covers this case. Hence 'solve Wahba's problem for ℓ=2' and 'complete characterisation of the Wahba problem' are unsupported. The efficiency gain over eigenvalue methods is asserted with no cost analysis or comparison. The formulas also involve quaternion square roots and a prior check of pairwise similarity.

failure_location.quote: The presented results offer a complete theoretical characterisation of the Wahba problem in quaternions

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract, introduction and conclusion. They should say that the paper characterizes the zero-cost minimizers of the two-observation Wahba cost for pairwise-similar data. They should state that the noisy case is not treated, and drop the unsupported efficiency claim or support it.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope (solution of Wahba's problem for ℓ=2, replacing eigen-methods) is much broader than the established result. That result is the zero-cost solution set under an exact pairwise-similarity hypothesis.
issues.title: Claims of solving Wahba's problem / complete characterization exceed the zero-cost, pairwise-similar case established
issues.why_classification: The theorems are untouched and a rewording fixes it, but the advertised regime (general minimization for two observations) is excluded. The paper's headline claim is therefore substantially weakened.
